articleTitle: Doppler Superpulse Processing for Improved Tomographic Characterization of Space Objects
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The tomographic perspective of 1D Doppler profiles formed from Range Time Intensity data enables 2D noncoherent imaging of rotating objects over wide aspect diversity. Tomographic reconstruction using these Doppler profiles obtained over a full rotation is known as Doppler Tomography. Doppler Tomography requires the target to be fully unresolved in range (occupy a single range bin). For large bandwidth regimes, the target is well-resolved in range and extends over multiple range bins. In making a single choice of range-bin for forming 1D Doppler profiles for tomographic reconstruction, Doppler tomography does not make use of all available bandwidth in the radar data and fails to address range migration. In this work, we propose Doppler superpulse processing, a strategy for fusing together DTIs formed across all range bins to create an enhanced Doppler versus time characterization data product. Doppler profiles obtained using superpulse processing preserve scatterers that are migrating across range due to the object's rotation. Our experiments with real compact range satellite radar data highlight the superior structural image quality of our Doppler superpulse tomographic reconstructions over those of conventional Doppler tomography.

articleTitle: Design of a Multilayer Microstrip Delay Line on a Water Based Composite Dielectric Medium
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The physical dimension of a microstrip delay line is known to depend upon the effective dielectric constant of the substrate. A higher dielectric constant is always advantageous for ensuring compact microstrip design while realizing large time delays such as those required for the phasing of antenna arrays at low radio frequencies. In this paper, we describe the design and development of a water-based composite dielectric medium optimized for achieving a higher effective dielectric constant in the frequency range of 30 - 360 MHz. Our tests of a prototype delay line (20 cm long) indicate an effective dielectric constant of a little over 26 with an insertion loss in the range of 0.1 dB to 0.9 dB.

articleTitle: Informed Deep Learning in Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Deep neural networks have demonstrated capability to solve challenging forward and inverse problems in electromagnetic metamaterials. However, they often require large quantities of data to achieve a given level of accuracy, which poses a data bottleneck issue and an initial delay in progress. Here we demonstrate two informed deep learning approaches which address the data bottleneck issue in metamaterial design. We show that through direct inclusion of physics in deep neural networks the required network size as well as the size of the dataset can be reduced compared to a vanilla feed forward neural network. We classify our informed deep learning approaches using a recently proposed taxonomy and give an outlook of this exciting field.

articleTitle: The Associated Hermite FDTD Method with Non-uniform Grid Scheme
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In order to solve the inefficiency problem of the FDTD method in computing fine structures, this paper proposes an AH FDTD method based on the non-uniform grid method. The main method used in this paper is to introduce a coordinate mapping relationship from non-uniform grid to uniform grid into AH FDTD, and derive the discrete update equation of electromagnetic field in AH domain in two-dimensional case. Finally, a simple example is given to illustrate the effectiveness, accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Fast Reconstruction of Optimal Pupil Apodization for Telescope Coronagraph Design Based on the Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Telescope coronagraph is an instrument designed to observe faint exoplanets located at very close proximities to their star by shielding the direct starlight and permitting planet light to pass through at an angle. In reality, however, aberrations and disturbances introduce phase variations and deteriorates the performance of the coronagraph. In this paper, an optimal telescope pupil apodization reconstruction scheme is introduced to restore the ideal pupil mode under such phase perturbations. Based on the eigenvalue problem solved by the method of moments, the proposed reconstruction scheme is applicable to telescope with an arbitrary pupil geometry. Numerical examples are given to demonstrate the application of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Radar-Vision Fusion for Vehicle Detection and Tracking
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The fusion of multi-sensors can prevent the drawbacks of a single sensor. In this paper, we propose a method to fuse tracked radar and vision targets. We use DBSCAN and SORT algorithms to detect and track radar targets and apply YOLOv5 and DeepSORT algorithms to generate vision target boxes. Then, we execute the time and spatial fusion for radar and vision targets. We conduct experiments on the Oxford Radar RobotCar Dataset and prove the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: Effect of Thermal Design Considerations of Implanted Antenna on Tissue Heating
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this study, a numerical parametric evaluation of an implanted dipole antenna system is utilized to investigate the amount of heat generation in the surrounding body tissues. The goal is to select the optimal implanted antenna design and test environment conditions which will contribute to the regulation of a steady state tissue temperature, with minimal effect on the surrounding tissue during monitoring and treatment processes. A multi-criteria decision-making process is applied using the design parameters namely, (i) body phantom type, (ii) body phantom size, and finally (iii) thermal boundary conditions. The findings suggested that the size of the body phantom used for the design, optimization, and testing of the implanted antenna has the largest effect on the temperature values and their distribution, regardless of tissue type. In addition, if the chosen phantom size is small, the selected thermal boundary condition parameters can have a significant effect on tissue temperature.

articleTitle: PSSFSS-An Open-Source Code for Analysis of Polarization and Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: PSSFSS is a free, open-source code for analysis and design of polarization selective surfaces (PSSs), frequency selective surfaces (FSSs), radomes, reflectarray elements, and similar devices. It is written in Julia, a recently developed language for high-performance technical computing. Its speed and ease of use make PSSFSS useful and accessible to both students and working engineers. This paper describes the design of PSSFSS and provides several examples of its use, with comparisons to results from other simulation tools.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Series Fed Antenna Array for Automotive 5G mmWave Communcations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents a circularly polarized series-fed microstrip patch antenna array for 5G mmWave communications to be used in the automotive industry. The proposed design operates in the 28GHz band (27.5GHz-28.35GHz) and can be implemented as a <tex>$2\mathrm{x}2$</tex> Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) antenna system in the front and back windshield to obtain larger coverage area around the vehicle and increase total throughput of the system or can be placed within a housing on the top roof. The array is designed using tapered line method where each element of the array is fed through different transmission lines with different impedance characteristics. The design is simulated using FEKO software and the results are presented and plotted in terms of reflection coefficient and total circular radiation pattern.

articleTitle: A Novel Broadband EBG Structure For Simultaneous Switching Noise Suppression
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a compact electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure for suppressing simultaneous switching noise (SSN) in high-speed circuits is proposed. At the bandwidth level of 0.35GHz to 20GHz, an ultra-wideband SSN suppression feature with a suppression depth of -40dB is achieved. The basic unit structure of the presented EBG is formed by etching an annular groove in the square patch and connecting the separated patches inside and outside the groove with a bridge adjacent to the end. An improved L-type bridge is used between the EBG units to further improve the EBG performance. Compared with the traditional L-type bridge, the suppression depth of the proposed electromagnetic bandgap structure is improved from -30dB to - 40dB. In addition, the time domain eye simulation results show that the structure has good signal integrity.

articleTitle: Multi-Fidelity Surrogate Modeling based on Numerical Eigenfunction Expansions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this work, a novel physics-based method for supplying low-fidelity models is studied. Specifically, numerical eigenfunction expansions are used to efficiently provide approximate electromagnetic solution data for a multi-fidelity (MF) surrogate optimization process. Based on our results, the proposed method can generate highly accurate MF models 3 times faster compared to state-of-the-art methods and with errors less than 3% when compared with full-wave solutions.

articleTitle: Enabling Deep Space Radar with EM Simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An upgrade to the Haystack Ultra-Wideband Satellite Imaging Radar (HUSIR) with a fifty-fold peak power increase is underway utilizing a vacuum power electron device for the W-band transmitter amplifier. This 17-dB sensitivity increase will extend the range of HUSIR capability to geosynchronous orbits (GEO). A single Communications and Power Industries (CPI) Gyrotron Traveling Wave Tube (TWT) design is expected to deliver 50-kilowatt peak power over the 92–100 GHz HUSIR bandwidth. A Raytheon Technologies solid-state amplifier will combine over 100 monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) devices to provide 100 watt peak power input for the GyroTWT. Modifications for the HUSIR radar transmitter, antenna feed, and transmit path are underway to accommodate the anticipated power increase. This paper highlights the contributions of EM modeling and simulation to this challenging development effort.

articleTitle: Discrete Taylor Transform and Inverse Transform in 2D and 3D
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In a recent contribution the Discrete Taylor Transform and Inverse Transform (D-TTIT) in one dimension was introduced, [1]. Based on a simple Toy Model, the current work extends the originally conceived D-TTIT to 2D. By analogy, the D-TTIT algorithm naturally extends from 2D to 3D. The presentation is based on a 2D discrete lattice, along with properly-chosen monomial products, <tex>$x^{m}y^{n}(m,n\in \mathbb{N})$</tex>, as initial continuous basis functions. The monomial products, sampled at the lattice points, generate a discrete basis <tex>$\vert\mathcal{B}^{m,n} >$</tex>. The main result in this work is the discovery that the dual basis associated with <tex>$\vert\mathcal{B}^{m,n} >$</tex> corresponds to the desired discrete mixed derivative operators <tex>$\vert \mathcal{D}^{m,n} >$</tex>. The constructed basis and dual basis satisfy the mutual orthogonality properly, and the resolution of the identity operator. Future work will examine the validity of these findings in curvilinear and logically rectangular coordinates.

articleTitle: An Automated Adaptive h-Refinement Technique for Solving SIEs with Nonconformal Meshes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An adaptive mesh refinement (h-refinement) technique is proposed to solve surface integral equations (SIEs) for electromagnetic scattering analysis. Based on the physics of the induced surface current and the geometry of the scatterer, rules are developed to identify regions for mesh refinement. Basis function with a phase factor are employed to better describe the phase variation of the current. In the proposed technique, the problem is first solved on a coarse mesh. Based on the coarse solution, regions are identified for refinement, which produces a nonconformal mesh. The discontinuous Galerkin integral equation method is then employed to solve the problem again on the nonconformal mesh for an improved accuracy. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Antenna with a Loading Metal Strip for GPS L1 band
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The paper presents a novel circular polarization(CP) antenna loading with a parasitic ring metal strip, which is designed for global positioning system (GPS) L1 band applications. The antenna consists of a defected ground plane with four arc-slots and a circular slot, a dielectric substrate, a parasitic ring metal strip, and a radiating patch (RP) with a arc-slot. By rotating the parasitic ring metal strip to opening slot on the RP, the antenna can be transformed from left-handed circular polarization (LHCP) to right-handed circular polarization (RHCP). The size of the antenna can be reduced by using slots on the ground. The simulation and optimization results show that impedance bandwidth of the L/RHCP antenna is over 100 MHz, and the axial ratio bandwidth is over 20 MHz.

articleTitle: Novel PM-Assisted Model of the Two-Layer Sub-Harmonic Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this paper, a new pm-assisted model has been developed for the already introduced two-layer sub-harmonic synchronous machine. This work aims to increase the torque-producing capability of the brushless wound rotor machines while keeping the use of rare earth magnets to a minimum. A 2D finite element analysis has been performed to validate the proposed model and compare the performance with the reference model. The results in the paper demonstrate that the proposed machine's average torque has increased.

articleTitle: Advanced hp-Refinement Methodology for Singular Solutions in Frequency-Domain Computational Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We present a multi-level anisotropic hp-refinement methodology for frequency-domain computational electromagnetics, based on a refinement-by-superposition approach. The methodology is applied for a higher order finite-element 2-D eigenvalue analysis of waveguides. Our methodology drives perfect exponential convergence with respect to the number of degrees of freedom for the accuracy of singular solutions, whereas the conventional alternative yields only algebraic convergence.

articleTitle: On the Spiral Resonator Arrays Size Analysis for Misalignment Compensation in Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: In this study the authors aim to use a metasurface as an additional component of a two-coil Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) system and to provide a robustness analysis to misalignment between the transmitter and the receiver coils. The analysis between metasurfaces of different size and their optimization performed to improve misalignment robustness is proved by numerical and easy circuital simulations with the aim of predicting the loads to be considered for the single unit-cell to properly control the WPT system and make it more tolerant to misalignment.

articleTitle: Integral Equation for Analyzing Neuron Response to Non-invasive Electromagnetic Brain Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Non-invasive electromagnetic brain stimulation uses electrodes and/or coils to induce an E-field in the brain and modulate its activity. To better understand the neurological effects of non-invasive electromagnetic stimulation we introduce an integral equation formulation for modeling non-linear response of neurons due to an incident E-field generated by electrode and coil sources. We approximate the new integral equation using boundary element method and compare its accuracy with an established finite element solver. Unlike previous approaches, this new formulation enables the modeling of action potential generation by an axon in a realistic head morphology. This method will aid the development of better neurological understanding, delineate the mechanisms by which electromagnetic stimulation engenders neuronal activity, and model local E-field coupling.

articleTitle: Efficient Upwind Schemes for Linear and Nonlinear Dispersive Maxwell's Equations on Overset Grids
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Overlapping grids are a powerful tool for representing the complex geometry inherent to many linear and nonlinear electromagnetic scattering problems. However, inter-grid interpolation is known to be potentially destabilizing in the context of wave phenomena. Upwind dissipation has become one of the most powerful tools to cure this instability, but unfortunately some of the original formulations were difficult to implement and expensive, particularly for complex material models. Here we present an optimized upwind scheme whose formulation enables a simple modular implementation so that it can be easily be applied even to complex models, and is computationally efficient in comparison to previous schemes.

articleTitle: Surface Propagation for the Mars Helicopter Mission using Parabolic Equation Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper will present the adaptation of proven earth propagation tools/model <tex>$s$</tex> to dramatically improve propagation predicts for the Mars Helicopter mission between the Rover “Perseverance” and the Helicopter “Ingenuity” on the surface of Mars. This Parabolic Equation method uses the complex topology of Mars and accounts for all four basic mechanisms that influence radio wave propagation: reflection, diffraction, penetration, and scattering.

articleTitle: Millstone Hill Radar L-Band Sensitivity Upgrade
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Efforts to increase the sensitivity of Millstone Hill Radar are nearly completed, with a new dual transmitter facility starting initial high power testing. The increase in average power is expected to double the sensitivity of the radar while providing a significant improvement in fault tolerance, overall robustness, and transmitter status monitoring.

articleTitle: Anomalous Current Spikes in the Locally Corrected Nystrom Discretization of Volume Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: A locally corrected Nystrom (LCN) discretization of a magnetostatic volume integral equation is presented. Anomalous current spikes are observed to occur when the underlying mesh uses tetrahedral cells. The mechanism for the anomalous current spikes is discussed, and mitigation of the current spikes through use of an LCN-to-Moment Method conversion is investigated. Results are presented validating that the LCN-to-Moment Method suppresses the anomalous current spikes.

articleTitle: Visualization of Electric and Magnetic Fields Inside Circular and Baffle Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This research presents an interactive software to visualize the electric and magnetic field distribution inside circular and baffle waveguides and cavities. This software features a user-friendly interface through which user can specify the design parameters such as dimensions, propagation mode (TE or TM), mode number, operating frequency, visualization plane angle (0° -360°). Both transverse and longitudinal field components can be visualized in vector, color contour or both. Field distributions can be displayed as static images or video animations using appropriate sequencing of computed field values. Moreover, this software is able to give all necessary warnings for invalid user input parameters. Mathematical expressions of the field components used in this software were derived from the classical solution of the wave equations using the separation of variables technique in cylindrical coordinates.

articleTitle: Low-Loss Wireless Implant Telemetry Using Magnetoinductive Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We introduce a novel wireless implant telemetry system that utilizes magnetoinductive waveguides (MIW) to break state-of-the-art boundaries in terms of: (a) transmission loss, and (b) bandwidth. Magnetoinductive waveguides rely on the careful design of a series of resonant loops, where excited current on the transmit loop leads to the current propagating as magnetoinductive waves to the receive loop. A MedRadio (401–406 MHz) MIW is shown to communicate with a 49.3 mm<sup>3</sup> implant at 1 cm depth with a transmission loss of only 19.4 dB and a bandwidth of 187.4 MHz. This represents an improvement of over 30 dB and 85 MHz over a similar Radio-Frequency (RF) based system. Notably, the reported MIW framework empowers a full wearable system that can be integrated into clothing to handle wireless nodes placed both on and inside the human body.

articleTitle: Ruggedized Reconfigurable Antennas through the Implementation of Innovative Mechanical Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The integration of compliant mechanisms with reconfigurable electromagnetics has the potential to greatly influence the next-generation of metamaterial and reconfigurable antenna systems. With the limitations of current reconfigurable technologies when deployed into harsh environments, compliant mechanisms can expand the available design space and provide robust solutions specifically targeted for ruggedization. This paper presents a compliant mechanism enabled dielectric rod antenna design that offers the ability to allow steering without a complex feeding network as well as being designed to withstand harsh environments. The aim is to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed solution in delivering reliable performance under challenging conditions.

articleTitle: Estimation of Dielectric Property for Biological Tissues by Multi-Frequency Approximation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper investigates a new method to calculate the dielectric property (DP) of biological tissues with the open-ended coaxial probes (OECP). The DP of tissues is a continuous function of frequency which can be represented with different dielectric relaxation models. Thus, the accuracy of DP measurements can be increased by enforcing such spectral continuity using the Cole-Cole model. A cost functional based on an admittance integral was calculated at the tip of the OECP. Then, Cole-Cole parameters <tex>$(\epsilon_{\infty}, \epsilon_{s}, \tau, \alpha$</tex> and <tex>$\sigma)$</tex> were applied into the admittance integral to solve a set of nonlinear equations. The OECP, biological tissues and calibration materials were simulated using Ansys HFSS simulation program from 0.5 to 6 GHz frequency range with 0.25 GHz steps (23 frequency points). Finally, the accuracy of results was compared with data obtained from literature.

articleTitle: X-Band Radar for Monitoring Space Debris
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Recent decades have seen the proliferation of debris in space from a variety of sources including on-orbit satellite collisions, intentional Anti-Satellite (ASAT) tests, and debris from routine satellite launches and payload deployments. The increase in the space debris population poses a risk to the operation of the International Space Station (ISS). The Haystack Ultra-Wideband Satellite Imaging Radar (HUSIR) is an X-band radar system that is uniquely capable to characterize this risk.

articleTitle: Transient Electro-thermal Analysis of the Bipolar Transistor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper describes the transient electro-thermal properties of the bipolar transistor by a two-dimensional transient electro-thermal simulation, in which model the coupled heat conduction equation and drift-diffusion equations are solved. The backward difference scheme with the second-order accuracy was used to discretize the time derivative. The increment of bipolar transistor temperature will affect the drift and diffusion of carriers and thus its electrical characteristics. Through the transient study of electro-thermal characteristics of the bipolar transistor, the influence of the self-heating effect on bipolar transistor characteristic has considered in amplification mode. The developed model and results obtained in this work can be used to optimize the thermal design of bipolar transistor.

articleTitle: Active Transmission-Type Metasurface for Linear-to-Circular Polarization Conversion at a Certain Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: An active transmission-type metasurface is presented, which is based on double metallic patches incorporated with active components of PIN diodes. It can be numerically obtained that the left circularly polarized(LCP) wave is transmitted at 4.3-4.48 GHz with a transmission coefficient of 25-46% under the OFF state of PIN diodes when the the structure is impinged by a <tex>$x$</tex> polarization. In addition, the ability of converting a y- polarized incident wave to a right circularly polarized(RCP) wave at the same frequency band is unambiguously exhibited with a transmission coefficient of 29.2-43.4% by actively controlling switchable PIN diodes. The proposed metasurface could be an active and dynamic approach to manipulate linear to circular(LTC) polarization conversion at a fixed frequency band.

articleTitle: Compressing a Fast Multipole Method Representation of an Integral Equation Matrix
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: It has been observed that the memory requirements associated with <tex>$H^{2}$</tex> representations of integral equation matrices can be reduced by incorporating translational invariance. This can be accomplished for a non-translationally invariant <tex>$\boldsymbol{H}^{2}$</tex> representation using a left/right iterative algorithm. In this paper, it is shown that a similar algorithm can also be used to compress an existing fast multipole method (FMM). It is observed that the iterative compression converges faster when used to compress an FMM than when it is applied to an <tex>$\boldsymbol{H}^{2}$</tex> representation.

articleTitle: Data Collection and Network Design for Deep Learning Based Metasurface Design
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper presents novel approaches to collect balanced high degree of freedom meta-atom patterns for machine learning models and a new design of neural network for meta-atom performance evaluation.

articleTitle: Fast Multi-source Electromagnetic Simulations using Augmented Partial Factorization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We describe full-wave single-shot computations for multi-source electromagnetic problems in both 2D and 3D using the “augmented partial factorization” method. This versatile approach bypasses unnecessary computations and avoids repetitions to achieve many orders of magnitude speed-up compared to conventional methods.

articleTitle: Noise Coil For Improving Sensitivity in a Fully Passive Bio-Magnetic Signal Detection System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Human emitted bio-magnetic signals are beneficial for several healthcare applications, yet they are difficult to capture due to their low magnitude. Overcoming limitations in the state-of-the-art, we previously reported a sensing system that can capture these signals in a non-contact, non-shielded, and low-cost manner. In this work, we take a major step further and demonstrate a noise coil subtraction scheme that successfully increases the sensitivity of the system. In vitro experimental results confirm that a reduced number of notch filters (10 vs. 13) are required to retrieve an 8.76 pT, 100–1000 Hz emulated evoked compound action potential (eCAP) signal with 30 minutes of averaging time when using the noise coil subtraction scheme. In the future, more advanced Digital Signal Processing (DSP) can be applied to adjust the level of noise for subtraction and further boost the sensitivity.

articleTitle: Dispersive Conductivity Conductor Simulation in Transmission Line with Compact 2-D FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The surface impedance boundary condition (SIBC) is reformulated for dispersive conductivity (DC) conductors, and combined with compact two-dimension finite-difference time-domain (C-FDTD) to analyze the dispersive characteristics of transmission lines. Compared with traditional constant conductivity (CC) model, the simulation results with proposed DC-SIBC agree much better with the measurements.

articleTitle: Scalable Snap Together Array Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: This paper details the design and measurement of a “Lego”-like array panel that can be connected like pieces in a puzzle. The geometric flexibility provides a way to produce much larger antennas and antenna arrays that would traditionally be limited by the size of a 3D printer's build plate. Furthermore, by changing the size of an aperture we can control the directivity, gain, power-on-target, and beam width resolution.

articleTitle: Case Study on Deployable Origami Antennas for Terahertz CubeSat Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: The increasing demand for high-speed space communication networks enabled by dense constellations has placed CubeSats as a key enabling technology for future wireless communication networks. An origami antenna for CubeSats operating in the Terahertz Band (0.1-10THz) has been proposed to provide a compact, high-gain wideband solution to meet the demands of ultra-wideband space networks without occupying space within the CubeSat's internal components. The origami horn antenna's initial form is compactly placed on the sides of a 1U CubeSat before deployment in space. One proposed mechanical risk of such origami antenna is potential errors in deployment or degradation of flanges over time. In this paper, the potential errors and degradation are simulated, and the antenna beam pattern, gain, and surface current are shown using the multilevel fast multipole method (MLFMM) computational method in Altair FEKO electromagnetics software.

articleTitle: Generative Neural Network Enables Reconfigurable Metasurface on Real-Time Free-Form Targets
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: We propose a generative neural network architecture that allows the inverse design of the reflective phases of units on a conformal, reconfigurable metasurface in real-time given free-form scattering requirements in different directions. The theoretical performance of this method is verified on a calculated dataset of a typical 2-D curved reflective surface.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Visualization Tools for Effective Undergraduate Education
publicationTitle: 2023 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES)
abstract: Visualization tools are essential for teaching core electromagnetic concepts to undergraduate electrical engineering students. We developed MATLAB tools for transmission type problems to enable students to understand how the input parameters affect the output in a 2D or 3D space. The applications explored include the design of coaxial cables, two-wire transmission lines, parallel-plate waveguides, as well as the electric reflection and transmission coefficients for parallel lossless or lossy slabs.
